messages.content: What is RAG?
RAG is a system architecture that combines information retrieval with large language model generation.
What are the main stages of a typical RAG pipeline?
A typical RAG pipeline includes document loading, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, optional reranking, context construction, and generation.
Why is retrieval important for RAG?
Retrieval is important because the language model cannot reliably use external knowledge if the relevant evidence is not retrieved.
What is a text embedding?
A text embedding is a numerical vector representation of text.
Why are embeddings useful for semantic search?
Embeddings allow systems to retrieve semantically similar documents even when the query and document use different words.
What happens when normalized vectors are compared using dot product?
When vectors are normalized to unit length, their dot product is equivalent to cosine similarity.
What is BGE-M3 used for?
BGE-M3 is used to convert queries and document chunks into embedding vectors for dense retrieval.
What is dense retrieval?
Dense retrieval represents queries and documents as vectors and searches for vectors that are close to the query vector.
What is FAISS used for?
FAISS is used for efficient similarity search over dense vectors.
Does FAISS generate natural language answers?
No. FAISS performs retrieval, while the language model generates the final natural language answer.
What is BM25?
BM25 is a classical lexical information retrieval algorithm.
What factors does BM25 consider?
BM25 considers term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization.
When is BM25 particularly useful?
BM25 is particularly useful for exact technical terms, names, identifiers, rare keywords, and specific phrases.
Why can BM25 perform well on exact technical terms?
BM25 uses lexical matching, so exact technical terms and rare keywords can strongly contribute to document relevance.
Why is whitespace tokenization problematic for Chinese BM25?
Chinese words are generally not separated by spaces, so whitespace tokenization may not provide useful word-level tokens.
What is hybrid retrieval?
Hybrid retrieval combines multiple retrieval methods, commonly dense retrieval and lexical retrieval.
Why combine FAISS and BM25?
FAISS captures semantic similarity while BM25 captures lexical matching, so they can complement each other.
Why should FAISS and BM25 raw scores not simply be added?
Their scores come from different algorithms and generally have different numerical scales.
What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion?
RRF is a rank aggregation method that combines multiple ranked lists using reciprocal rank contributions.
What is the RRF formula?
For a document at rank r, its RRF contribution is 1 divided by k plus r.
What value of k is commonly used for RRF in this project?
The project uses k equal to 60.
Why does RRF use ranking instead of raw retrieval scores?
RRF uses rankings because different retrieval systems can produce scores with incompatible numerical scales.
What is reranking?
Reranking is a second-stage retrieval process that refines the ranking of candidate documents.
Why is reranking performed after first-stage retrieval?
First-stage retrieval efficiently produces a candidate set, while reranking uses a more expensive model to improve precision among those candidates.
What is a cross-encoder reranker?
A cross-encoder reranker receives a query and document together and directly models their interaction to estimate relevance.
What is BGE-Reranker-v2-M3 used for?
It is used as a multilingual reranking model to refine the ranking of candidate documents.
Why is a reranker normally applied to only a small candidate set?
Cross-encoder reranking is computationally more expensive than first-stage retrieval, so it is normally applied to a relatively small candidate set.
What does Recall@K measure?
Recall@K measures whether a relevant document appears within the top K retrieved results.
What does MRR measure?
MRR measures how highly the first relevant result is ranked using the reciprocal of its rank.
What is the difference between Recall@K and MRR?
Recall@K checks whether a relevant result appears within the top K, while MRR also considers how highly the first relevant result is ranked.
What is faithfulness in RAG evaluation?
Faithfulness measures whether the generated answer is supported by the retrieved context.
Can retrieval quality be evaluated independently from the LLM?
Yes. Retrieval can be evaluated independently using metrics such as Recall@K and MRR.
Which retrieval method is likely to be useful for a query containing an exact rare technical term?
BM25 is likely to be useful because it performs lexical matching and benefits from exact and rare terms.
Which retrieval method is likely to help when the query and document use different wording but have similar meanings?
Dense retrieval is likely to help because it retrieves documents based on semantic similarity.
Why is RRF useful when combining FAISS and BM25?
RRF combines their rankings without requiring their raw relevance scores to have the same numerical scale.
What happens if the embedding model is changed after building a vector index?
The vector index may need to be rebuilt because the stored vectors belong to the original embedding space.
Does BM25 require training a neural network?
No. BM25 is a classical lexical retrieval algorithm and does not require training a neural network during retrieval.
What is the typical pipeline for hybrid retrieval followed by reranking?
FAISS and BM25 retrieve candidates, RRF combines their rankings, a reranker refines the candidate ranking, and the final chunks are passed to the LLM.
Why should retrieval evaluation and generation evaluation be separated?
Retrieval evaluation measures whether relevant evidence was retrieved, while generation evaluation measures the quality and faithfulness of the final answer.
Who invented the Transformer architecture?
I don't know.
